The owner's statement may withdraw a resolution. It may not make one, break a tie, or supply a direction. GET /v1/reports/assets. Serde field order is the reading order and a contract test asserts it on the raw bytes: confidence, then cash, then positions with oldest_price_date, then total, then the account rows.

The two halves stay apart. Cash is Money — exact, the journal's own figures, grouped by declared class per currency. Positions are CalcMoney — quantity times the quote the journal holds — carrying the oldest price behind the total, which is the weakest link, plus a per-holding as_of. Only then the total, and it is CalcMoney so the type itself says a market can move it. Nothing is FX-converted: every total is per currency, because converting would put a rate inside the exact half.

One fold: asset_snapshot takes the balances answer's own rows, copies them once, and folds every class total, side total and grand total from that vector. No second read of the journal, no second selection of accounts. make arch passes.

The class stays opaque to the core, structurally: iaam-core depends on no workspace crate, so the class arrives as an Option<String> code and grouping by equality is all the core can do. None is its own group, never a default.

Prices come from the journal's own PriceBoard, and PriceBoard::observe became the single definition of 'this event carries a price', with projection::advance pointed at it — so a report cannot value a holding from a price the projection would not have recorded. An unpriced holding is absent from the total, never zero, and says so as a caveat.

Deviation from the bead's design, flagged: positions are priced from the journal board rather than the returns pipeline. PUT /v1/accounts/{id}/declarations. Three optional keys, each an object carrying 'stated', borrowed literally from AccountTransferPartnersDto one noun over: the key's absence means he has not mentioned it and the stored value stands; {stated: false} means he states none and it is cleared; {stated: true, ...} sets it. Re-pointing an identity is accepted, and the response says what it did not do. The evidence settled it: the events table records a fact against an account id and a free source label, and no column or event kind records the external identity in force when the row arrived — provider arrived in migration 0020, on accounts, and the journal is immutable in the database by trigger, so nothing can be backfilled to make one. The journal therefore cannot answer 'do facts exist under the old identity'. A refusal would have to be conditioned on 'does this account have facts at all', which is a different claim: it refuses an account whose whole history was typed in by hand under no identity, and still does not answer the question anyone asked.

So the response publishes what can be known — facts_recorded, named for the account and not the identity — plus a closed not_done register naming three things it did not do, including that no fact records the identity it arrived under. The displaced identity is returned, for the debuggability reason ADR 0004 §1 gives for storing the printed value at all.
